Its connection to graciousness and kindness is tied to the values of compassion, generosity, and love instilled within the faith. These characteristics have been exhibited by numerous figures throughout Islamic history, including the Prophet Muhammad PBUH and his blessed companions. Thus, naming a child Ruqaiya serves as both a tribute to these profound values and a reminder for them to uphold and display these qualities throughout their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ruqaiya holds deeper significance as it relates to the Islamic concept of being God-conscious and compassionate towards others. The title "Ruqaiya" is derived from the Arabic word "Raqqa" which means "neck or throat". The Imam of Medina, Ibrahim al-Nakh'i, reported that a person once asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about the best character, to which he replied, "The best of character is to abandon what Allah hates, to love what Allah loves, and to follow the Prophet Muhammad's traditions and sunnah" [Bukhari].
